turns.message: BACK AT IT!! Right that was honestly the perfect restart run. Legs feeling a bit sorry for themselves but in the best way possible 😅🙌

Right so I'm going to say it, that ridge section was genuinely spectacular this morning. The light was doing something extraordinary over Ilkley. Felt like we earned every metre of it.
Honestly yes! Rafe you should have had your camera out on that descent 📸 Tom did you clock the segment time on that ridge? I feel like we got a decent one in
Yeah, segment's up. Personal best for three of us. Lads can check Strava.
The ridge section had 340m of elevation gain in the last 2.4km. Good route.
Solid effort from everyone. I would note the flat section along the reservoir was the correct choice for warm-up given the conditions.
Tom you DESIGNED this group with Nadia right haha, so technically this whole thing is your fault 😂 three years of Sunday suffering
Ha! Three years ago this September actually, Tom turned up at the same parkrun as me for like four consecutive weeks and eventually I just said we should make it official 😂💪

haha that tracks 😅 so cafe then? I'm on for a flat white if anyone wants to join 🙏
Doing the reservoir loop on the way back. Could add the eastern ridge if people have legs. More interesting than the main path.

I will head back directly.

Reservoir plus eastern ridge then Malt Shovel. That's a plan.

Wednesday went well. Pace was better than Sunday. Less stopping.
Tom that is literally the nicest thing you have ever said 😂 but yeah honestly I think I need to do this more regularly? Like one Sunday a month was fine but now I'm wondering why I wasn't doing more

planted_challenges.evidence_span: one Sunday a month was fine but now I'm wondering why I wasn't doing more

planted_challenges.evidence_span: Cass and I were at the back for most of the Chevin climb on Wednesday, which I'm choosing to frame as 'taking in the scenery', and we had about twenty minutes of completely excellent conversation about exactly nothing.

turns.message: haha yes!! Rafe is very good company when you're suffering uphill 😂 are we doing a route this Sunday? What are we thinking?

Oh that one is gorgeous! I vote yes 🙏 Tom? You happy with Wharfedale?
Wharfedale works. Decent technical section on the descent.
I can confirm Sunday. I would suggest a 7:30am start to avoid the afternoon hikers on that route.
7:30 works for me! 🙌 Rafe are you in? You were saying on Wednesday that you might have a deadline?

Right so I submitted the piece Thursday evening, very much under the wire, so yes I am absolutely in. My reward to myself for that particular ordeal is a long Sunday run followed by something substantial at the pub.
Yes!! Okay so Sunday 7:30, Wharfedale, Rafe buys the first round 😂🎉
Can we try the eastern variation on the descent? Better terrain.
The eastern variation adds 2.1km and 60m elevation. Viable.

I'll put it in the chat Friday morning 🙌 Tom do you want to lead on the descent section since you know that terrain better? 💪
Yeah. I'll set the line on the technical section.
Oh and can we do cafe after this time? Pretty please 😅☕ Rafe I know you want the pub but brunch first?
Here's the thing, Cass, I will compromise on brunch if there is eventually a pint involved somewhere. The two are not mutually exclusive.

sessions.topic: Wet trail run debrief and Yuki's slip

turns.message: Lads. Conditions out there. Everyone make it back okay?
I am SOAKED and my shoes are probably never the same again but honestly that was exhilarating 😂💦 Yuki are you alright? That slip looked pretty scary
Made it! Only slightly died on that descent haha 😅 Yuki seriously are you okay?
I am fine. Bruised knee, nothing structural. The surface was significantly worse than the elevation profile suggested.
Right so that descent, and I say this as someone who has written about adversity for a living, was genuinely treacherous. The wet clay section past the stile had no business calling itself a trail.
Yuki honestly thank goodness you're okay, that looked really bad 😬 I know it sounds boring but if you're running those wet descents regularly it's worth thinking about shoe grip 💙
My road shoes have insufficient traction on wet clay. Noted.

planted_challenges.fact_value: was using road shoes on all terrain; after this slip acknowledged the inadequacy and bought proper trail shoes
planted_challenges.evidence_span: My road shoes have insufficient traction on wet clay. Noted.

turns.message: I would second that. The grip differential between road and trail shoes on saturated ground is significant. It is not a marginal consideration.
Trail shoes. Non-negotiable in these conditions.
Yuki I can send you the ones I use if you want a recommendation? 😊 I switched about a year ago and honestly never looked back
Yes. Send the model.
Okay who is coming to the cafe?? We've all earned it this morning honestly 😂 I'm buying the first round of coffees as a 'we survived' celebration ☕
In for coffee.
Absolutely in. Here's the thing, I took one genuinely brilliant photo of the mist over the valley from the top before my fingers stopped cooperating. Going to warm up with a double espresso.
Yes!! Yuki you coming? 🙏
Not today. I need to get home.

planted_challenges.fact_value: prefers to skip post-run social stops and go straight home; finds the social time draining

If the swelling increases or the joint feels unstable, that warrants assessment. Otherwise RICE protocol is appropriate.
Understood.
Leo on call as always.
Right so, are we doing something flatter next Sunday? I've had my fill of near-death experiences on clay for one week.

sessions.prior_session_summary: Wet Wharfedale run. Yuki slipped on a clay descent in road shoes, bruised knee. Group agreed trail shoes needed. Yuki declined post-run cafe as usual. Rafe proposed an easier route next time.

sessions.topic: Half marathon sign-up and GPS watch debate

NADIA YES!!! 🎉🎉🎉 we are doing this together oh my god!! This is so exciting!!

Leo yes! Okay you and I need to talk training plans seriously 😅 I know you're the sensible one here
Lads, anyone else thinking about the Harrogate? Good excuse for some proper long Sundays.

Rafe YES do it!! And Tom?? We could all do it haha 🙌

I just run by vibes haha 😅 does that make me team Tom or team Rafe?
Team no-overthinking.
Team aesthetics. Which frankly is the superior approach to most things.

sessions.topic: 21km long run debrief and Rafe cramping episode

turns.message: 21km in the bag!! 🙌 honestly that was a tough one but SO good. Rafe you okay after that calf cramp situation? That looked painful 😬

Right so the cramp at km 17 was, to put it diplomatically, humbling. I had been anticipating a triumphal finish and instead spent five minutes doing an undignified roadside stretch while Tom pretended not to notice.
Noticed.
Oh no Rafe 😭 are you okay now? You were going so well before that haha

I am fine, thank you. My ego is the primary casualty. Nadia however gave me a very thorough breakdown of what I'd done wrong nutritionally, which I suspect she'd been waiting to deliver for some time.

I HAVE been waiting to deliver it, I won't lie 😂 Rafe you always go straight to the pub after long runs and every time you cramp on anything over 12km. I've been watching this pattern for months. You need electrolytes and food before any alcohol, it's just physiology

planted_challenges.fact_value: Rafe always goes straight to the pub after long runs and repeatedly cramps; Nadia has been observing this pattern for months without stating it until now
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Rafe you always go straight to the pub after long runs and every time you cramp on anything over 12km. I've been watching this pattern for months.

turns.message: Inadequate sodium replacement post-exertion causes cramping. The research on this is consistent.
Correct. I would add that alcohol is a diuretic and actively impedes recovery. I would not recommend it within two hours of any effort over 15km.
Right so I'm receiving this lecture from three separate directions simultaneously, which feels disproportionate but is probably deserved. Fine. Electrolytes first. Then pub.
Smart.
Rafe this is growth!! 🎉 seriously though, are you sure you're okay? Your face when it happened was not great haha

Here's the thing, it was significantly painful in the moment, yes. But I took the electrolyte tablet Nadia had in her pack and the recovery was noticeably faster than usual. Which I will grudgingly admit supports her point.

planted_challenges.fact_value: shifted from going straight to the pub after long runs to accepting electrolytes and food first; acknowledged the change works
planted_challenges.evidence_span: I took the electrolyte tablet Nadia had in her pack and the recovery was noticeably faster than usual. Which I will grudgingly admit supports her point.

turns.message: Thank you Rafe I'll take that grudging admission 😂 honestly you should start carrying your own electrolytes on anything over 15km, it's not complicated
A simple sodium-potassium tablet or appropriate sports drink at the halfway point would prevent this entirely.
Lads, did everyone hit their long run target? Nadia, you were going well in that second half.
21.3km!! Personal long run best, honestly can't believe it 🥹🙌 four months ago I thought 15km was a big deal
Nadia that's incredible!! 🎉 we are SO ready for Harrogate haha
Good elevation data from today. I have updated the Strava segment.
I would note my heart rate was slightly elevated on the second climb. I will reduce intensity on next Sunday's long run.
Right so, pub? I will have an electrolyte drink first, in full compliance with medical guidance, before ordering anything else.
Fair.

sessions.topic: Tom's negative split discovery and post-run pub consensus

turns.message: Lads. Did something different today. Held back the first 8km intentionally. Negative split the second half. Felt completely different.
Tom WHAT I noticed you were holding back early and was going to ask if you were okay!! How did it feel?? 🤔
Better. Got this from a coaching podcast. Whole episode on effort distribution. Changed my view on it.

planted_challenges.evidence_span: Got this from a coaching podcast. Whole episode on effort distribution. Changed my view on it.

turns.message: Right so this is Tom admitting that a podcast changed his mind, which is more than I thought I'd hear this decade.
Data is data. Even if it comes on audio.
Tom has EVOLVED haha 🎉 seriously though that's really interesting, did you end up with a better overall time?
2 minutes faster over 16km than the same route in September. With less perceived effort in the last 3.
That is consistent with the research on pacing strategy. Negative splits outperform even-effort by approximately 2-4% in recreational runners.
I concur. Training at controlled effort in the first half also reduces cortisol load and preserves glycogen more efficiently.
Okay I'm definitely trying this next Sunday now 👀 Tom you should do a session on this for the group sometime honestly

Here's the thing, I ran almost entirely by feel today and the second half was where the route revealed its best qualities. The light on the moors at that point was something. I'm less convinced by the optimisation angle but more convinced by the experience.
Rafe you had your camera out again haha 😅 we saw you stopping for about three minutes near the top
Wholly worth it. Three minutes of artistic investment for an excellent photograph.
Cost you the segment.
I have made my peace with it.
Okay pub after? This is a proper post-long-run Sunday and I think we've all earned it 🍺 right? Who's in?
In.
Absolutely. Here's the thing, I have been very virtuous on the electrolytes front today. I consider this a qualifying performance for a pint.
Yes haha!! 🙌 Leo? Yuki?
I will join briefly. I will not be drinking.
I have things to do this afternoon.

planted_challenges.evidence_span: I have things to do this afternoon.

turns.message: Fair enough! Five out of six isn't bad 😄 Yuki see you next week

sessions.topic: Pre-race taper week and Leo's hamstring concern

turns.message: ONE WEEK until Harrogate!! I'm honestly oscillating between very excited and mildly terrified 😂🏃‍♀️ everyone else feeling this way?
Taper week. Easy runs only. Legs need to be fresh.
I am SO nervous haha but also so ready?? Nadia this is happening! 🎉
Right so I am not running it in the end, scheduling issues, but I will be at the finish line with adequate hydration and a sign. You have my full moral support.
Rafe you are an actual angel thank you 😭💙 Leo you still in?

Leo 😬 okay first, how bad? Second, have you been doing literally any stretching?
It is a grade one strain at most. Nothing structural. And I will admit I have not been rigorous about stretching. I have consistently deprioritised it.
Leo I have told you this MULTIPLE times 😅 it takes ten minutes! Ten minutes after every run and this doesn't happen!
Nadia's right. Have been doing the ten minute stretch since she told me last spring. Zero issues.

Yes. I understand the data now, clearly. I intend to make it non-negotiable going forward. Whether I can run Harrogate is a separate question, I am going to assess how the hamstring responds to a short easy run tomorrow.

The hamstring attaches at the ischial tuberosity. Grade one strains typically resolve in 7-10 days with appropriate management.
Thank you, Yuki.
Okay so three years of running together and we've ended up with Tom converting to negative splits and Leo finally doing stretches. Honestly this group has come a long way since that first parkrun 💙
Nadia recruited half this group from parkrun.

The fact that you two basically invented this group and are still both here making it happen is genuinely lovely haha 😊
It's a good group.

turns.message: WE DID IT!!!!! 🎉🎉🎉 Harrogate Half is DONE!! 2:04:23 and I am absolutely broken and also crying a little bit, I won't lie 😭🏅
NADIA YES!!! 🎉🎉🎉 I'm so proud of us!! 2:06:51 for me and I literally don't care I'm so happy!! 💪
1:51:12. Negative split worked. Second half 3 minutes faster than the first. Lads.

RIGHT SO I have been standing at the finish line for an hour with this sign and I have just witnessed what I can only describe as an extremely moving series of personal victories. Well done all of you. Well done.
Rafe I saw the sign from about 200m out and it made me run faster I think 😂 also it said 'GO RIDGELINE RUNNERS' in massive letters which is exactly the correct energy
I crossed in 2:01:44. The hamstring held. I completed the full post-race stretch protocol on the grass over there. For the record.
Leo!!! 😭 so proud of you oh my god!! And the stretching!! This is a huge day 🙌
Leo doing stretches at the finish line is my new favourite image haha 😂💙
I ran the Yorkshire Trail 25km this morning. 3:14:07. Good conditions.
Solid. That course is technical.
The first descent was icy in places. Grip from the trail shoes was adequate.
Yuki oh wow you ran a different race today?? That is amazing!! Trail 25km is no joke 🙌 how are your legs?
Tired. I will manage.

Right so, what's the post-race plan? I have been standing in a field for an hour and I believe I have earned a proper Sunday lunch somewhere. Ideally something with a beer garden and a menu that doesn't involve protein bars.
Malt Shovel. They do food. Good pub.

planted_challenges.evidence_span: Malt Shovel. They do food. Good pub.

turns.message: Yes!! Although haha can we do cafe for coffees first? I need caffeine before anything else 😅 then pub?

I need to get back.

turns.message: I will join for the cafe. I will not be staying for the pub.
Fair enough. Cafe first then Malt Shovel for anyone staying.
Here's the thing, I was at the finish line, I did not run a race, and I am still absolutely in for both. This feels like the correct reward structure.
Winter running schedule, shall we talk about that next week? I'm thinking we plan some longer training runs through November 💪 this group is too good to just go back to casual Sundays now 🏃‍♀️
